hints: Use $\vec{OD} = \vec{OC} - \vec{DC}$ to find the position vector of $D$.
walkthrough:
Find the displacement vector $\vec{AB}$ from $A(2, 1, -3)$ to $B(0, 4, 1)$:
$$\vec{AB} = \vec{OB} - \vec{OA} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$$

ai_rubric.Using Position Vectors: Uses correct vector relation e.g. $\vec{OD} = \vec{OC} - 3(\vec{OB} - \vec{OA})$ (M1). Obtains $\vec{OD} = 3\mathbf{i} - 11\mathbf{j} - 10\mathbf{k}$ (A1).

hints: Form vector equations for diagonals $AC$ and $BD$.
Equate components to find the intersection point $P$, or use the trapezium diagonal ratio $AP : PC = 1 : 3$.
walkthrough:
Find the vector equation of diagonal $AC$:
$$\vec{AC} = \vec{OC} - \vec{OA} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ -2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ -3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\mathbf{r}_{AC} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix} + \lambda\begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ -3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$$

Find the vector equation of diagonal $BD$:
$$\vec{BD} = \vec{OD} - \vec{OB} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -11 \\ -10 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -15 \\ -11 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\mathbf{r}_{BD} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} + \mu\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -15 \\ -11 \end{pmatrix}$$

Use similar triangles in trapezium $ABCD$:
Since $AB \parallel DC$ and $DC = 3AB$, triangles $\triangle PAB$ and $\triangle PCD$ are similar with linear scale factor $3$.
Therefore, the point of intersection $P$ divides the diagonal $AC$ in the ratio $AP : PC = 1 : 3$, meaning $\lambda = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

ai_rubric.Using Position Vectors: Forms vector equation of at least one diagonal (M1). Obtains equations for both diagonals or uses ratio from similar triangles (A1). Equates components and solves for parameter (DM1). Obtains parameter value $\lambda = 1/4$ (or equivalent) (A1). Obtains $\vec{OP} = \frac{3}{4}\mathbf{i} + \frac{1}{4}\mathbf{j} - \frac{7}{4}\mathbf{k}$ (A1).

hints: Evaluate $\vec{BA} \cdot \vec{BC}$ and the moduli of both vectors to calculate $\angle ABC$ using $\cos(\angle ABC) = \dfrac{\vec{BA} \cdot \vec{BC}}{|\vec{BA}||\vec{BC}|}$.
walkthrough:
Determine the vectors originating from vertex $B$:
$$\vec{BA} = -\vec{AB} = -\begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -3 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\vec{BC} = \vec{OC} - \vec{OB} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ -2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ -6 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Calculate the lengths of both vectors:
$$|\vec{BA}| = \sqrt{2^2 + (-3)^2 + (-4)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 16} = \sqrt{29}$$
$$|\vec{BC}| = \sqrt{(-3)^2 + (-6)^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{9 + 36 + 1} = \sqrt{46}$$

Calculate $\cos(\angle ABC)$ using the scalar product formula:
$$\cos(\angle ABC) = \dfrac{\vec{BA} \cdot \vec{BC}}{|\vec{BA}||\vec{BC}|} = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{29}\sqrt{46}} = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{1334}} \approx 0.219034$$

Take the inverse cosine to determine the angle:
$$\angle ABC = \arccos(0.219034) \approx 77.347^\circ \approx 77.3^\circ \quad (\text{or } 1.35 \text{ radians})$$

ai_rubric.Using Scalar Products: Identifies direction vectors $\vec{BA} = 2\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} - 4\mathbf{k}$ and $\vec{BC} = -3\mathbf{i} - 6\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$ (B1). Applies scalar product correctly to get $8$ (M1). Divides by product of moduli $\sqrt{29}\sqrt{46}$ and takes arccos (M1). Obtains $77.3^\circ$ or $1.35$ radians (A1).
